certification.name: PyTorch Core: Practical ML & Neural Networks

tasks.name: Use common layers and reason about shapes
Use embeddings, normalization, and registered modules

concepts.name: Subclassing `nn.Module`
concepts.description: Custom neural networks normally subclass `nn.Module`, call `super().__init__()`, and assign child layers as module attributes.

concepts.name: `forward` and calling the model
concepts.description: A Module defines computation in `forward`, while normal user code should call `model(x)` so Module hooks and wrapper behavior are respected.

concepts.name: `nn.Linear`
concepts.description: `nn.Linear(in_features, out_features)` applies an affine transformation to the last input dimension.

concepts.name: `nn.Sequential`
concepts.description: `nn.Sequential` chains modules in order so each module receives the previous module output.

concepts.name: Common activation modules
concepts.description: `nn.ReLU` applies `max(0, x)`, while activations such as GELU provide alternative nonlinearities used in many modern architectures.

concepts.name: Flattening feature dimensions
concepts.description: `nn.Flatten(start_dim=1)` commonly flattens all non-batch dimensions while preserving dimension 0 as the batch axis.

concepts.name: `nn.Conv2d`
concepts.description: `nn.Conv2d` expects image-like input with channels in the second dimension for batched tensors: `[N, C, H, W]`.

concepts.name: Pooling
concepts.description: `nn.MaxPool2d` downsamples spatial dimensions by taking local maxima over a window.

concepts.name: `nn.Embedding`
concepts.description: `nn.Embedding(num_embeddings, embedding_dim)` is a learnable lookup table that maps integer indices to embedding vectors.

concepts.name: Dropout
concepts.description: `nn.Dropout(p)` randomly zeroes elements with probability `p` during training and behaves as an identity transform during evaluation.

concepts.name: Batch normalization mode behavior
concepts.description: BatchNorm modules can track running statistics and use training-versus-evaluation mode differently, so `train()` and `eval()` matter for inference correctness.

concepts.name: `ModuleList` and module registration
concepts.description: `nn.ModuleList` stores a list of child modules while keeping them registered with the parent Module.

concepts.name: Parameters and `state_dict`
concepts.description: `model.parameters()` iterates registered Parameter objects, while `model.state_dict()` returns a mapping of registered parameters and persistent buffers.

questions.explanation: Custom neural networks normally subclass nn.Module, call super().__init__(), and assign child layers as module attributes. Registered child modules and parameters are discovered by methods such as model.parameters() and state_dict(). Keeping layers only in an ordinary Python container can bypass module registration unless you use containers such as ModuleList or ModuleDict.
hints: Registered child modules and parameters are discovered by methods such as model.parameters() and state_dict().

questions.explanation: nn.ModuleList stores a list of child modules while keeping them registered with the parent Module. Use ModuleList when you need list-like iteration over a dynamic number of layers but cannot express the computation as a simple Sequential chain. A plain Python list of layers is not a substitute when you need automatic parameter registration by the parent Module.
hints: Use ModuleList when you need list-like iteration over a dynamic number of layers but cannot express the computation as a simple Sequential chain.
